# opencode-advisors-v2

Native OpenCode V2 advisor/watchdog plugin. Attaches passive reviewer personas to an OpenCode session. Each reviewer observes completed primary-agent model steps, independently checks for mistakes or drift, and emits at most one concise note (nit / concern / blocker).

## Install

**Git (recommended):**

```jsonc
// ~/.config/opencode/opencode.json (or project opencode.json)
{
  "plugins": [
    {
      "package": "github:0x4nur4g/opencode-advisors-v2",
      "options": {
        "enabled": true,
        "defaultModel": "anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5#medium",
        "advisors": [
          { "name": "Skeptic", "instructions": "Challenge assumptions..." }
        ]
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

Works on any machine with git access; pin a commit with `github:0x4nur4g/opencode-advisors-v2#<commit>` (or track the default branch with `github:0x4nur4g/opencode-advisors-v2#main`).

**Local checkout:**

```bash
bun install          # dev dependencies only
```

```jsonc
{
  "plugins": [
    { "package": "/absolute/path/to/opencode-advisors-v2", "options": { "enabled": true } }
  ]
}
```

This minimal form activates the built-in Skeptic advisor bound to the configured default model (see Configuration).

The plugin loads from TypeScript source with no build step: the OpenCode
directory loader resolves the repo-root `index.ts` (a 3-line re-export of
`src/index.ts`), with `package.json` beside it as the loader requires. The
`exports` field points tooling and import consumers at the same root
`index.ts`; `bun run bundle` remains available as optional local tooling.

The plugin is **disabled unless `enabled: true`** is set. There is no implicit activation from a sidecar config file.

## Compatibility

OpenCode v2 line only — v1 is not supported.

Status: **experimental** (v0.1.0). The plugin is written against the v2 plugin
API; plugin loading is live-verified on opencode v2.0.5 (serve probe,
2026-09-17), and the raw `{ id, setup }` object-export contract it uses has
been verified from the beta line (beta-18286) through v2.0.5. Some host
surfaces the plugin relies on (agent transform on plugin-defined agents, the
session context hook) are not live-verified on every runtime build — pin a
commit for stability.

## Configuration

Key options (the full option set is defined in `src/options.ts`):

| Key | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | `false` | Must be `true` to activate |
| `defaultModel` | — | `provider/model#variant` |
| `advisors` | built-in `Skeptic` | Array of persona definitions; omitted key → built-in default; explicit array (incl. `[]`) replaces it entirely |
| `review.mode` | `"async"` | `"async"` or `"sync"` |
| `review.maxParallel` | `3` | `1..8` |
| `review.timeoutMs` | `30000` | `1000..120000` |
| `delivery.immuneTurns` | `3` | `0..20` |
| `delivery.wakeOnTerminalBlocker` | `true` | Blocker on an idle-terminal session wakes it with the note; `false` queues instead |
| `delivery.hardInterruptBlockers` | `false` | Experimental opt-in. Blocker on a RUNNING session: interrupt the in-flight turn, then wake the stopped session with the note. The host documents no deadline/cancellation guarantee for `ctx.session.interrupt`; the bare call can stall review processing |

Out-of-range values are rejected with a path-specific error, not silently clamped.

When the `advisors` key is omitted and the plugin is enabled, one built-in
advisor — **Skeptic** — is registered automatically, bound to `defaultModel`
and marked `[builtin]` in `advisor-status` output. An explicit `advisors`
array always replaces the default entirely (it is never merged), and an
explicit empty array (`[]`) registers no advisors at all — a deliberate
opt-out.

## Reviews and Controls

Reviews are fully automated and passive: session hooks observe context, updates
queue inside the runtime, thresholds drain the queue, and advisory notes are
delivered as synthetic session messages (`ctx.session.synthetic`). No tool call
or manual trigger is involved.

Advisory notes post with an explicit `delivery` mode. `queue` deliveries
promote FIFO at the end of the next drain (one head promotes when the drain
would otherwise end), so a queued advisory enters the transcript and the
outbound model context of the successor turn, ordered after pending user
turns; `steer` promotes at the next safe provider-turn boundary. An
independent `resume` wake policy is selected by the severity/state matrix —
the host default is never relied on. A failed post is retained as bounded
post-only retry state and re-posted on later session events (no regeneration,
FIFO: one attempt at emission plus at most 3 bounded retries — 4 total post
attempts — before abandonment). Emission dedupe state commits only after
durable admission, so a lost post never silently suppresses the note. See
[Attention parity and blocker interruption](#attention-parity-and-blocker-interruption-product-requirement-2026-09-24)
for the full severity/state matrix and the blocker interrupt flow.

Advisor sessions are created with the advisor's configured model bound
explicitly at session creation (per-advisor override, else the plugin
default) — hosts otherwise resolve a session's run model from the
session/config default, which would leak the primary model into advisor runs.

The only user-facing controls are two administrative commands:

| Command | Effect |
|---|---|
| `advisor-status` | Reads in-memory runtime state for the current session and posts a bounded status notification (status, queue depth, per-advisor model, health, metrics). |
| `advisor-reset` | Clears the current session's advisor state (buffers, queue, dedupe, cooldown) and posts a deterministic confirmation. |

Both run directly in the plugin process: they read or mutate in-memory state and
post a notification-style message with `resume:false`, so it appears in the
session inbox without scheduling any model execution — invoking either command
performs zero primary-model generation. They stay silent when invoked without a
session (headless runs). There are no model-callable advisor tools and no manual
review command.

## Attention parity and blocker interruption (product requirement 2026-09-24)

**Requirement:** every advisor note must be at least as visible/attended as a
normal chat message to the session it reviews — never a lower-priority,
invisible inbox artifact. Blockers may additionally interrupt the running
target session, experimental and opt-in (see below).

### Delivery matrix

| State | nit | concern | blocker |
|---|---|---|---|
| Running | steer | steer | steer (interrupt-then-wake when `hardInterruptBlockers: true`) |
| Idle terminal | resume | resume | resume when `wakeOnTerminalBlocker`; else queue |
| Idle incomplete | resume | resume | resume |
| User interrupted | queue | queue | queue |
| Cooldown | steer/resume by state | steer/resume by state | steer/resume by state |

- `steer` = admitted at the next safe provider-turn boundary; the note keeps
  its synthetic advisor provenance and does not impersonate a user or system
  message — the host picks the boundary, which is not necessarily the same
  scheduling or authority as a normal user message. A `queue` delivery
  promotes behind pending user turns, which live observation on 2026-09-24
  confirmed is strictly lower ordering.
- `resume` = wake the idle session so the note becomes the next turn's input
  (one drain, exactly one successor provider turn).
- Only user-interrupted sessions queue; an idle-terminal blocker with an
  explicit `delivery.wakeOnTerminalBlocker: false` also queues — every other
  note steers or resumes by state, cooldown included.
- Blocker + running + `delivery.hardInterruptBlockers: true` (experimental,
  default `false`): the plugin calls `ctx.session.interrupt` first and then
  posts the note with `resume: true` (interrupt FIRST, note SECOND). When the
  call resolves, the interrupted turn ends and the note wakes the session as
  the next turn's input — one successor turn. The reverse order is forbidden: a
  note posted before the interrupt stays inbox-only indefinitely (silent loss),
  observed in the 2026-09-24 single-file host-ordering probe on opencode
  v2.0.15, which covers only the resolved path. The host documents no
  AbortSignal/deadline/cancellation guarantee for this RPC: the call is a bare
  await and can stall review processing.

### Interrupt loss, as the user sees it

The in-flight turn is aborted: unsettled tool calls fail with
`Tool execution interrupted`, partial assistant text is retained, the execution
outcome is `interrupted`, and then the resumed turn attends the note. The
interrupt fires `session.execution.interrupted` with `reason: "user"` — from the
host's perspective it is indistinguishable from a user stop, and the plugin
treats it the same way (further steers are suppressed until the next execution
start; the armed cooldown bounds the next interrupt).

### Authority boundary

Notes travel only through `ctx.session.synthetic`: the transcript types them as
synthetic messages with the advisor's XML attribution in the body
(`<advisory advisor="..." severity="...">`). The plugin never writes
system/developer authority, never injects a `session.prompt` user message, and
never impersonates user consent.

### Residual non-parity (accepted, by design)

Only user-interrupted sessions deliberately stay `queue` (plus the explicit
`delivery.wakeOnTerminalBlocker: false` case for idle-terminal blockers):

- **User interrupted** — after the user stops a turn, advisories must not
  restart it. This is a user-preserved safeguard.

Cooldown is not a delivery exception: it arms only after a resolved opt-in hard
interrupt and suppresses repeated hard INTERRUPTS only. Notes keep their
state-appropriate steer/resume during cooldown. Queued notes are not lost: they
promote on the next actionable turn instead of waking the session.

### Rate and cost

Each wake is one successor provider turn (≈ 1 model request) plus the reviewer
generation that produced the note. A hard interrupt resolved in ≈ 10 ms in the
single v2.0.15 host-ordering probe (2026-09-24) — a dated observation of the
resolved path, not a general latency ceiling (the call has no host deadline).

Loop bounding:

- the cooldown (`immuneTurns`, default 3) arms only after a resolved opt-in hard
  interrupt and decrements on step ends; it suppresses repeated hard INTERRUPTS
  only — notes are never queued or demoted by it;
- severity-escalation dedupe is bounded (4096 entries) and suppresses identical
  notes; only an escalated severity re-emits. Paraphrased notes are not deduped
  and can wake again;
- the noise filter drops low-signal notes, reviewers see their own prior notes
  (`priorAdvice`), and repeated reviewer failure halts the advisor;
- the interrupt path additionally requires blocker + running + a steered
  non-user-interrupted row + no active cooldown, so the interrupt ceiling is ≈ 1
  per cooldown window per session.

Honest limit: **there is no hard per-session reviewer/wake/spend cap.** The
exact-note dedupe bound above is the only repeat suppression; paraphrased notes
can wake again, and the model unit price is unknown, so spend is not
quantified.

### Historical backlog (not retroactive)

This change affects only NEW emissions. Already-parked inbox notes (~10-12
across 14 sessions as of 2026-09-24) are NOT auto-drained: there is no polling,
no scheduler, no timers. They promote only if their session naturally runs
again.

### Scope

The mechanism is session-level and identical for worker/lead/orchestrator
target sessions: the plugin reviews any session in the registered directory and
posts to THAT session. There is no automatic cross-session parent broadcast in
the host — a completed child's wake is attended in the child's own transcript;
parent-side visibility is outside this plugin.

### Testable acceptance criteria

- fake blocker control (running session, `hardInterruptBlockers: true`):
  `session.interrupt` fired, the note is in the transcript, and the resumed
  turn contains a model ACK;
- fake concern and nit controls (running session): no interrupt; nit still
  steers at a boundary;
- idle-terminal concern/nit: the session wakes and the note is the next turn's
  input;
- user-interrupt control: no interrupt, no wake (queued);
- repeated identical note: deduped, no second interrupt;
- completed-child wake: attended in the child's own transcript.

## Bundle

```bash
bun run bundle   # optional local tooling: dist/index.js
bun run typecheck
bun test
```

The script is named `bundle`, not `build`: lifecycle-named scripts (`build`, `prepare`, `preinstall`, `postinstall`, `install`, `prepack`) trigger the host's git-dependency preparation path during Git-hosted plugin installation, which is not lifecycle-safe; `bundle` avoids it.

## API Exports

```ts
import plugin, { parseOptions, AdvisorRuntime } from "opencode-advisors-v2"
```

The root `index.ts` re-exports all three from `src/index.ts`.

- `default` — the plugin object `{ id: "opencode.advisors", setup }`; this is what the loader registers
- `parseOptions(raw)` — strict validation; throws on unknown keys, out-of-range values, malformed model refs
- `AdvisorRuntime` — runtime class for lifecycle, event consumption, and status (embedding/advanced use)

### Deferred

- `followPrimary: true` is accepted in config but advisors using it are skipped until model-specific session reuse is proven.
- `WATCHDOG.yml` roster discovery (`src/roster.ts`) is implemented but not wired into the runtime (Phase 2).

### Advisor tool capabilities

Every advisor gets the read-only investigation tools `read`, `glob`, and
`grep` as agent capabilities. `bash`, `edit`, `write`, and all mutating tools
stay denied. Passive reviews do not invoke tools; a tool-capable review loop
remains deferred.

Network tools are opt-in per advisor:

```jsonc
{ "name": "Researcher", "network": true }
```

`network` defaults to `false`. The advisor reviews untrusted transcript
content; with network egress, injected instructions in that content can
steer it to exfiltrate file secrets via fetch URLs or search queries
(bounded tool input/result values are now included — full reviewer
visibility — with best-effort credential-value redaction applied to the
whole transcript before dispatch). Opt in only if you
accept that risk. Networked advisors get a policy addendum restricting
what they may place into queries and URLs.

The passive review path is tool-free. It uses `ctx.session.generate()` with an
explicit no-tools instruction because advisor agents may still advertise read
tools. Read-only permissions remain registered for advisor agents, but passive
reviews do not invoke them.

## Privacy

A cross-provider advisor means your transcript data reaches another provider. Reviewer transcripts include bounded (2000-char) tool input and output values for every step — full session visibility by design (USER DIRECTIVE 2026-09-24: "reviewer sees everything"; this reverses the fail-closed exclusion shipped in `10b0abb`). `redactSecrets` still masks recognized credential VALUES before dispatch (API keys, tokens, env-var assignments, URL userinfo, and Basic credentials in curl `-u`/`--user` argv and `Authorization: Basic` headers), binary content is still skipped, advisory self-exclusion (loop prevention) is unchanged, and the plugin does not log full prompts by default. Redaction is pattern-based and best-effort: unrecognized credential shapes are NOT masked, and Basic header values below 8 characters are not redacted.

## Known Limitation

Advisor sessions are created as root sessions because the exposed V2 plugin `create` omits `parentID` and `title`. Deterministic session IDs prevent unbounded duplication. Upstream child-session support is the intended fix.

# Troubleshooting & Operational Lessons

Findings from debugging an opencode v2 chat failure that traced to a manually-created shim/compat file, not the plugin itself. Update this doc every time a new failure mode is found.

---

## Incident 2026-07-26: opencode v2 chat stopped responding

### Symptom

User sends any message in opencode v2 chat -> no response. The model generates output (logs show `stream providerID=... modelID=...`), but the chat UI never receives it.

### Root cause

A shim file at `~/.config/opencode/plugins/advisors-v2.ts`:

```ts
export { default } from "<repo>/src/index.ts"
```

This hand-made file re-exported the plugin's **TypeScript source** through the legacy generic file-plugin loader. The premise that made it fail was the shim, not `.ts` loading: opencode v2's plugin loader **does** execute TypeScript source (since beta-18286; this repository loads its `index.ts` entry with no build step). A file discovered under `~/.config/opencode/plugins/` is validated as a generic plugin module and must default-export an object with a `server()` method — the v2 `{ id, setup }` contract this plugin uses does not provide one.

### Two failure modes, same cause

1. **Hard crash (yesterday, 25 occurrences):** When the v2 plugin was loaded via the `plugins` config key with `package` pointing at the raw `.ts`, the loader partially loaded it. The tool registry got `undefined` tool descriptors. When the model tried to respond, the registry snapshot blew up:
   ```
   TypeError: t is not an Object. (evaluating '"~standard" in t')
     at ../plugin/src/v2/effect/internal/tool.ts:207:25
     at ToolRegistry.snapshot -> SessionContext.select -> SessionRunner.runSteps
   ```
   Each crash = one chat message that never got a response. 25 crashes between 22:18–22:50 on 2026-07-26.

2. **Clean rejection (after config revert):** After reverting `opencode.json` to remove the `plugins` key, the shim file remained in `~/.config/opencode/plugins/`. The loader now rejects it cleanly on every startup:
   ```
   failed to load plugin path=file:///.../advisors-v2.ts
   error="Plugin ... must default export an object with server()"
   ```
   This is non-fatal but noisy - and confusing because the plugin appears "registered" (file in plugins dir) but never actually loads.

### Fix applied

```bash
rm ~/.config/opencode/plugins/advisors-v2.ts
```

### Correct installation

Load the package through the V2 `plugins` configuration. No build is required for live loading; do not create a legacy file-plugin shim.

```jsonc
{
  "plugins": [
    {
      "package": "/absolute/path/to/opencode-advisors-v2",
      "options": { "enabled": true }
    }
  ]
}
```

---

## Rules to avoid repeating this

### 1. Do not install a V2 promise plugin through a legacy file shim

A file discovered under `~/.config/opencode/plugins/` is validated as a generic plugin module with a `server` export. This package uses the V2 promise contract (`id` + `setup`) and belongs in the V2 `plugins` configuration.

### 2. No build step is required for live loading

The v2 loader executes TypeScript source (since beta-18286). `bun run bundle` remains optional local tooling (`dist/`); it is not required to load the plugin. The `bundle` script is available as:

```json
"scripts": {
  "typecheck": "tsc --noEmit",
  "test": "bun test",
  "bundle": "bun build src/index.ts --outdir dist --target node --format esm"
}
```

### 3. Smoke-test the entry before loading

Before loading the plugin into opencode v2, verify the entry actually default-exports a valid v2 plugin:

```bash
bun -e 'import("./index.ts").then(m => {
  const p = m.default;
  if (typeof p?.setup !== "function") throw new Error("not a valid v2 plugin");
  console.log("ok", p.id);
})'
```

If this fails, do not configure the package. If the log says `must default export an object with server()`, the package was sent through the legacy file-plugin loader; remove the file shim and use the V2 `plugins` configuration.

### 4. Check the log before declaring "chat is broken"

The log at `~/.local/share/opencode/log/opencode.log` tells you exactly what's wrong. Key grep patterns:

```bash
# Plugin load failures (non-fatal but noisy)
grep "failed to load plugin" ~/.local/share/opencode/log/opencode.log | tail

# Chat-blocking crashes (fatal - these are why chat doesn't respond)
grep "Failed to drain Session" ~/.local/share/opencode/log/opencode.log | tail

# Per-day count
grep "2026-07-27" ~/.local/share/opencode/log/opencode.log | grep -c "Failed to drain Session"
```

If `Failed to drain Session` count is > 0 for today, chat is broken by a tool registry crash. Find the `cause=` in the log - it's almost always a plugin returning a bad tool descriptor.

### 5. v1 plugins in the `plugin` array fail v2 schema validation - that's expected

Under opencode v2, all v1-style plugins in the `plugin` array will warn:
```
failed to load plugin target=oh-my-openagent@latest cause=SchemaError(Missing key "effect", "setup")
failed to load plugin target=ponytail.mjs cause=SchemaError(Expected object, got async function)
```

These are **non-fatal** - opencode v2 continues without them. Don't chase these warnings unless you actually need the plugin working under v2. They're v1 plugins running under a v2 loader; they need to be ported to v2's plugin contract to load.

### 6. The `plugins` config key (plural) is v2-only; `plugin` (singular) is v1

- `opencode.json` `"plugin": [...]` - v1 array of paths/packages, loaded by v1 loader
- `opencode.json` `"plugins": [{ "package": "...", "options": {...} }]` - v2 array with options, loaded by v2 loader

Mixing them causes confusion. The v2 `plugins` key accepts `package` pointing at a directory path or npm package name; the entry must default-export the v2 `{ id, setup }` contract. TypeScript source is supported (since beta-18286; no build step required).

### 7. When chat stops responding, check these in order

1. `ps aux | grep opencode` - is the process running?
2. `tail -30 ~/.local/share/opencode/log/opencode.log` - what's the last activity?
3. `grep "Failed to drain Session" ~/.local/share/opencode/log/opencode.log | tail` - tool registry crash?
4. `grep "failed to load plugin" ~/.local/share/opencode/log/opencode.log | tail` - plugin load failure?
5. `ls ~/.config/opencode/plugins/` - any stray shims?
6. `curl -sS --max-time 5 <provider baseURL>/v1/models` - is the model provider reachable?

### 8. The V2 entrypoint default-exports a literal `{ id, setup }` object

`src/index.ts` ends with:
```ts
export default plugin
```
where `plugin` is a literal object with `id` and `setup` — no `define()` wrapper and no `@opencode-ai/*` runtime import. This form is runtime-verified from beta-18286 through v2.0.5. Without `setup`, the loader rejects the plugin. A `server()` error instead indicates that the legacy file-plugin loader was used.

### 9. Keep a known-good `opencode.json` backup

The backup `opencode.json.bak` was critical for diagnosing this incident - it showed the `plugins` key that caused the registry crash. Always keep a backup before editing plugin config:
```bash
cp ~/.config/opencode/opencode.json ~/.config/opencode/opencode.json.bak
```

### 10. Test in a clean directory

Stale session state in `~/.local/share/opencode/storage/` can mask or cause issues. When smoke-testing the plugin live, start opencode v2 in a fresh directory:
```bash
mkdir -p /tmp/advisors-smoke && cd /tmp/advisors-smoke && opencode2
```
This avoids picking up session state from other projects.

## Standard verification loop

Before declaring the plugin ready to load into opencode v2:

```bash
cd <repo>

# 1. Unit tests
bun test

# 2. Typecheck
bun run typecheck

# 3. Bundle (optional local tooling)
bun run bundle

# 4. Smoke-test the entry
bun -e 'import("./index.ts").then(m => {
  const p = m.default;
  if (typeof p?.setup !== "function") throw new Error("invalid v2 plugin");
  console.log("ok", p.id);
})'

# 5. Load live through the V2 plugins configuration (README install path)
cd /tmp && opencode2
# In chat: /api/plugin  ->  should list opencode.advisors
# Send a message ->  should respond, no "Failed to drain" in log
```

If any step fails, **do not** create a legacy file-plugin shim. Fix the failure first.

## Plugin is `active` but no advisor agents or commands appear

Symptom: the plugin reports `active`, but the `advisor-status` and
`advisor-reset` commands are missing and no advisor agent is registered.

Cause: every advisor needs a resolvable model reference at setup. The catalog
snapshot reads the provider list first, and that list omits config-defined
providers entirely and can lag models populated after plugin setup (for example
models added by a discovery plugin). Unresolved references skip the advisor, and
setup stops before registering agents, the session hook, and commands.

Fix behavior: when the provider-list snapshot cannot resolve a configured
reference, the plugin retries the direct model lookup on a bounded window
(fresh transform reads with backoff for up to 20 s), so late-populated models
still register; a model that never appears is skipped safely.

Check, in order:

1. Service log skip lines — `Skipped "…": no model configured (no_model state)`
   or `model variant not found in catalog` — they name the advisor and reason.
2. `GET /api/model` — confirm the referenced provider/model (and `#variant`
   when the ref has one) exists.
3. Reload — editing the plugin registration in `opencode.json` hot-reloads
   plugins without a restart; if the service keeps the old behavior, restart
   it (restarts drop running sessions).

## Runtime compatibility

Live-acceptance + v2.0.15 event note: see [docs/LIVE-ACCEPTANCE-20260924.md](./docs/LIVE-ACCEPTANCE-20260924.md) — on v2.0.15 `session.tool.called` carries the call id under `id` with no `name`; fixed in `10b0abb` (decode `session.tool.input.started` for the name; key `called`/`success`/`failed` by `id`). Tool-only steps now deliver reviews, and the reviewer transcript carries tool identity + outcome + bounded input/result values (full reviewer visibility, user directive 2026-09-24; recognized credential values masked by `redactSecrets`).

## Changelog

- 2026-07-27: Initial doc. Recorded incident where `advisors-v2.ts` shim pointed at unbuilt `.ts` source, causing `Failed to drain Session` crashes and silent chat failure. Fix: remove shim, build plugin before re-adding.

behavior and root-session limitations. This document is the canonical
reference for what the plugin can and cannot do at each integration layer.

## Root-Session Limitation

The most significant architectural limitation of the current plugin API
is the absence of child session support.

### What this means

- Advisor sessions are created as **root sessions** with deterministic IDs
- They appear in the session list alongside user sessions
- They cannot be cleaned up on plugin dispose (no `session.remove`)
- They cannot be titled or labeled as advisor sessions
- They cannot be linked to their parent primary session

### Why deterministic IDs help

The plugin uses SHA256-based deterministic IDs:
```
ses_advisor_<sha256(directory + workspaceID + pluginID + slug).slice(0, 32)>
```

This prevents unbounded duplication - the same project+persona always
reuses the same session. Without this, every plugin reload would create
a new root session.

### What's needed

Exposing `parentID` in `ctx.session.create` and adding `ctx.session.remove`
would let advisor sessions be children of the primary session, visible
only in context, and cleanly removable. This is the #1 upstream request.

---

## Phase 5: Read-Only Investigation Tools - Implemented (Gated)

Advisors receive **read-only investigation tools** (`read`, `glob`,
`grep`) as agent capabilities. The passive review path does not invoke them;
a tool-capable review loop remains deferred. Network tools
(`websearch`, `webfetch`) are **opt-in per advisor** via `network: true`
(default `false`).

### Capability set

| Capability | Default | Opt-in |
|---|---|---|
| `read`, `glob`, `grep` | allowed | always on |
| `websearch`, `webfetch` | denied | `network: true` |
| `bash`, `edit`, `write`, everything else | denied | never |

Permission rules are deny-all first, then explicit allows (host matching
is last-match-wins, so unmatched tools are dropped from the model's tool
list entirely, not merely denied).

The passive review path does not invoke these tools. It uses
`ctx.session.generate()` with an explicit no-tools instruction. Read-only
permissions are reserved for a future tool-capable review loop.

### Why network tools are opt-in

The advisor reviews untrusted transcript content. With network egress,
injected instructions in reviewed content can steer the unsupervised
advisor to fetch attacker-controlled URLs whose query strings carry
repository context or file secrets it just read — reviewer transcripts
include bounded tool arguments and results (full reviewer visibility,
user directive 2026-09-24), and `redactSecrets` masks recognized
credential shapes before dispatch (API keys, tokens, env-var assignments,
URL userinfo, Basic credentials in `-u`/`--user` argv and
`Authorization: Basic` headers — Basic header values below 8 characters
are not redacted) but arbitrary content is not fully sanitized. Local
read tools cannot
leave the machine; network egress is a side effect. Opting in accepts
this risk; the policy addendum then instructs the advisor to prefer
known documentation domains and to never place file contents or secrets
into search queries or URLs.

### Stance on mutating tools

`bash`/`edit`/`write` stay denied unconditionally: the advisor is an
automated, unsupervised reviewer that fires every review cycle. A
reviewer that mutates state is a second unsupervised actor, not an
advisor. The plugin likewise
registers no model-callable advisor tools: its only controls are the
`advisor-status` and `advisor-reset` administrative commands, which read or
mutate in-memory state and post synthetic notifications without any model
generation.

# Upstream API Proposals

Implementation-ready proposals for OpenCode V2 plugin API improvements
needed for full advisor functionality. Each proposal includes the current
gap, the concrete API change, and the impact on the advisor plugin.

Status: **mixed** — section 3 shipped; sections 1, 2, 4 proposed.

---

## 1. Child Session Lifecycle

**Current gap:** Plugin context `session.create` omits `parentID` and `title`.
Advisor sessions are created as root sessions, cluttering the session list
and preventing cleanup. Internal V2 session service already supports
`parentID`, `title`, remove, list, message, and context.

**Proposed API:**

```ts
// Plugin context additions
ctx.session.create({
  id?: string,
  agent?: string,
  model?: Model.Ref,
  location?: { directory: string; workspaceID?: string },
  parentID?: string,    // NEW: link to parent session
  title?: string,       // NEW: display name
})

ctx.session.remove({ sessionID: string })           // NEW
ctx.session.context({ sessionID: string })           // NEW
ctx.session.message({ sessionID: string, messageID: string })  // NEW
```

**Impact on advisor plugin:**
- Advisor sessions appear as children of the primary session
- `remove()` enables cleanup on plugin dispose or session delete
- `context()` enables reliable resync of advisor transcript
- `message()` enables optional child-work inspection
- Removes root clutter: deterministic IDs prevent duplication, but visible
  root sessions are confusing to users

**Implementation note:** The internal `SessionService` at
`packages/core/src/session/` already has `create`, `remove`, `get`,
and `messages`. The plugin host subset at
`packages/core/src/plugin/host.ts` omits these. Exposing them through
the plugin context is a host-side change only.

---

## 2. Exact Generation Usage and Cost

**Current gap:** `ctx.session.generate()` returns `{ text: string }` only.
No token usage, cost, or model attribution. The advisor plugin must estimate
usage from character counts (4 chars/token) and label all numbers as estimates.

**Proposed API:**

```ts
interface GenerateResult {
  text: string
  usage: TokenUsage       // NEW
  cost?: MoneyUSD         // NEW
  model: Model.Ref        // NEW
}

interface TokenUsage {
  inputTokens: number
  outputTokens: number
  cacheCreationTokens?: number
  cacheReadTokens?: number
}

interface MoneyUSD {
  amount: number   // in USD, e.g., 0.001234
}

ctx.session.generate({ sessionID, prompt }): Promise<GenerateResult>
```

**Impact on advisor plugin:**
- Replaces estimated token counts with exact usage
- Enables accurate per-review cost tracking
- Enables cost-conscious model selection (e.g., prefer cheaper model for
  nit-level reviews)
- Removes the "estimated" label from all metrics
- Enables attribution of usage to the owning primary session

**Implementation note:** The transient generation path at
`packages/core/src/session/generate-node.ts` already has access to
provider response metadata including usage. The return type needs to be
widened to include this data.

---

## 3. Direct Command Callbacks — Shipped

**Shipped reality:** the command transform already accepts direct callback
commands, and the advisor plugin uses that form for its two administrative
controls:

```ts
ctx.command.transform((draft) => {
  draft.add({
    name: "advisor-status",
    description: "Show advisor status: active advisors, models, health, queue depth",
    execute: async (context) => {
      // read in-memory runtime state for context.sessionID
      // then deliver a deterministic notification (no model turn):
      await ctx.session.synthetic({ sessionID, text, description: "advisor-status", resume: false })
    },
  })
})
```

`advisor-status` and `advisor-reset` read or mutate in-memory runtime state
synchronously, then post a bounded, deterministic notification via
`ctx.session.synthetic`. They never call `session.generate`, never create
sessions, and never post instruction text. Reviews themselves stay fully
passive: session hooks observe context, updates drain at thresholds, and
advisory notes arrive as synthetic messages. The commands are administrative
controls, not a review trigger. Passive reviews use tool-free
`ctx.session.generate` with an explicit no-tools instruction.

**Superseded proposal (2026-07-24 era):** earlier planning assumed command
transforms were static prompt templates, that a slash command could not return
live data without an LLM, and that the plugin therefore had to expose an
`advisor_status` tool costing a model turn to call. It proposed a
`commands.update` mutator whose handler *returns* content, plus a
`command.hook("execute")` event surface. Both are superseded: the callback
command form above is already shipped, and command `execute` return values are
not a documented output channel, so the plugin delivers output through
synthetic messages instead.

**Impact on advisor plugin (shipped):**
- Status and reset answer instantly from in-memory state, with no model cost
- The command surface is the only control path; passive reviews do not invoke tools
- Proposed `commands.update`, return-content, and `command.hook("execute")`
  surfaces are not needed and are not part of the plan

**Implementation note:** see `src/commands.ts` for the shipped registration.

**Non-generating delivery:** command invocations run only the plugin callback —
no host-side prompt or wake is issued by the command path. `ctx.session.synthetic`
schedules session execution unless `resume: false` is passed, so all command
notifications post `resume: false` (the same pattern the host TUI uses for its
own non-generating notes). The earlier observation of an "extra agent run" after
a command invocation is attributable to default-resume synthetic acks waking the
session, not to the command path.

---

## 4. Stable Hook Naming

**Current gap:** The V2 plugin guide calls the mutable pre-dispatch hook
`request`. The validated target exposes and invokes the mutable hook as
`context`. The naming divergence between documentation and the validated
host contract creates confusion and fragility.

**Proposed resolution:**

Align docs, types, and runtime on a single canonical name. Recommend
`context` (matching the installed package) and deprecate `request`
in the docs.

**Impact on advisor plugin:**
- Removes the need for a hook-name adapter
- Eliminates the risk of compilation failure on API change
- Simplifies onboarding for new plugin authors

**Implementation note:** The divergence is in the plugin guide docs at
`v2.opencode.ai/docs/build/plugins`. The package types are authoritative.
Update the docs to match the package.

---

## 5. Root-Session Limitation Summary

These proposals are ordered by impact on the advisor plugin:

| # | Proposal | Impact | Complexity |
|---|----------|--------|------------|
| 1 | Child session lifecycle | High - removes root clutter, enables cleanup | Low (host-side only) |
| 2 | Exact generation usage | High - removes estimates, enables cost tracking | Low (widen return type) |
| 3 | Direct command callbacks | Shipped — status/reset run without an LLM | Low (callback form already available) |
| 4 | Stable hook naming | Low - cleanup, already works | Low (docs only) |

---

## Runtime compatibility notes (plugin-side, no host change needed)

- Session-event payload fields may arrive wrapped under `event.data`; the
  runtime normalizes that shape and the legacy top-level shape into a single
  payload view (`data` fields win per key; the top-level `type` is preserved).
- `ctx.session.synthetic` delivery is never left to the host default: advisory
  posts pass an explicit `delivery` (`queue` = FIFO promotion at the end of the
  next drain — one head promotes when the drain would otherwise end, so a
  queued advisory lands in the transcript and outbound model context of the
  successor turn, after pending user turns; `steer` = promote at the next safe
  provider-turn boundary) plus an independent `resume` wake policy from the
  severity/state matrix. A failed post is retried post-only on later session
  events (one attempt at emission plus at most 3 bounded retries — 4 total
  post attempts — before abandonment) and emission dedupe commits only after
  the post is admitted.
- Advisor model binding happens at the create boundary, not at generate: hosts
  resolve a session's run model as `session.model ?? config default`, so
  advisor sessions are created with the configured provider/model/variant
  passed as the create-time `model` field. `ctx.session.generate` accepts only
  `sessionID` + `prompt` and cannot carry a model.

|------|---------|-------|----------------|
| `WATCHDOG.md` | Reviewer-only **attention guidance** (Markdown) | MVP (discovery) | **Wired** via `discoverWatchdog()` in runtime |
| `WATCHDOG.yml` | **Roster**: named advisors, models, instructions, tool declarations | Phase 2 | **Deferred** — `src/roster.ts` is implemented but not imported by the runtime |

The distinction matters: `WATCHDOG.md` is raw reviewer attention data
discovered as escaped XML blocks; `WATCHDOG.yml` is structured config that
defines _which advisors exist_ and _how they behave_.

## Discovery Order

Both file types are discovered **broad-to-specific** in this order:

1. `~/.config/opencode/WATCHDOG.{yml,yaml}` - user-level global
2. `WATCHDOG.{yml,yaml}` and `.opencode/WATCHDOG.{yml,yaml}` from **project root** toward the **session directory** - project-level descending
3. `~/.config/omp/WATCHDOG.{yml,yaml}` - OMP paths (**only** when `guidance.ompPaths: true`)

The same `.yml` and `.yaml` extensions are equivalent; `.yml` is preferred
for canonical paths. WATCHDOG.md discovery uses the identical walk (implemented
in `src/guidance.ts`).

## WATCHDOG.yml Schema

### Top-level keys

```yaml
enabled: true          # boolean - whether the roster is active (default: true)
instructions: |        # string - shared instructions for all advisors
  These are concatenated broad-to-specific.
  They form the baseline before persona-specific instructions.

advisors:              # array - named advisor definitions
  - name: "security"   # string (required) - display name, slugified for id
    enabled: true      # boolean (default: true) - per-advisor toggle
    model: "anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-20250514"  # string - provider/model ref
    instructions: |    # string - persona-specific instructions
      You are a security reviewer...
    tools:             # string[] - declarations rejected in this release
      - read
      - grep
      - glob
```

### Merge Semantics

Files are merged in discovery order (broad -> specific):

| Key | Merge rule |
|-----|------------|
| `enabled` (top-level) | **Last file wins** - the most specific file's value |
| `instructions` (shared) | **Concatenated** in discovery order with `\n\n` separator |
| `advisors[*].enabled` | **Last file wins** for same slug |
| `advisors[*].model` | **Last file wins** for same slug |
| `advisors[*].instructions` | **Concatenated** for same slug across files |
| `advisors[*].tools` | **Last file wins** for same slug |

Persona text **extends** rather than replaces the safety baseline. A more
specific file's shared instructions are appended after the broader file's
instructions; a more specific file's persona instructions for the same slug
are appended after the broader file's persona instructions.

### Unknown Keys

Unknown keys at any level produce **path-specific warnings** in the
`diagnostics` array. They are never silently dropped. The file is still
parsed - unknown keys do not cause a hard failure.

### Malformed Values

Malformed values (wrong types, missing required fields) produce **path-specific
errors** in the `diagnostics` array. The affected entry is skipped (if it's
an advisor) or the entire file is skipped (if the top-level structure is
invalid). A bad project config cannot kill the session.

## Tool Grants - Validation Only

**The initial release grants no workspace tools.** Tool grants in
`WATCHDOG.yml` are parsed and validated but **not applied**:

- **Empty `tools: []`** - explicit "no tools" - accepted with no warning.
- **Any non-empty list**, including `read`, `grep`, and `glob`, is **rejected** and recorded in `unsupportedTools` until Phase 5's lifecycle and permission gates are met.
- Mutating and unknown tool names are rejected by the same rule.

The `hasUnsupportedTools()` and `advisorsWithUnsupportedTools()` helpers let
the caller decide whether to warn or error. The roster still loads; tools
are just flagged.

### Why Validation-Only?

Current OMP can broaden a persona's grant through `WATCHDOG.yml`, including
mutating tools. That grant bypasses the primary approval wrapper and is
explicitly dangerous. This V2 plugin intentionally starts with transcript-only
review. A later read-only investigation mode requires clean child-session
lifecycle and verified permission behavior.

## @path Imports

**NOT expanded in the MVP (Phase 2).** The MVP omits `@path`
imports and YAML roster parsing.

- Lines matching `@path/to/file` (or the `@import` alias) at the start of a
  line are **kept as literal text** inside the escaped
  `<review-attention>` block. They are never resolved against the
  filesystem, never read, and never stripped.
- No containment, cycle-detection, depth, or size guarantees apply to
  imports because no import resolution happens in the MVP.
- Phase 2 will add import expansion together with the containment, realpath,
  cycle, depth, and aggregate-size guarantees described here. Do not rely on
  `@path` references reaching reviewer models in the MVP.

## Canonical Example

### `~/.config/opencode/WATCHDOG.yml` (user-level, broad)

```yaml
instructions: |
  Always review for security issues first.
  Flag any hardcoded secrets or exposed credentials.

advisors:
  - name: "Security"
    model: "anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-20250514"
    instructions: |
      You are a security reviewer. Check for:
      - Hardcoded secrets
      - Insecure cryptography
      - Missing input validation

  - name: "Performance"
    enabled: false
```

### `WATCHDOG.yml` (project root, more specific)

```yaml
instructions: |
  This is a TypeScript project. Flag `any` types and missing exhaustiveness checks.

advisors:
  - name: "Security"
    model: "anthropic/claude-opus-4-20250514"
    instructions: |
      Additionally, check for prototype pollution and unsafe DOM manipulation.
```

### Merged Result

- **Shared instructions**: "Always review for security issues first..." + "This is a TypeScript project..."
- **Security advisor**: `enabled: true`, model `anthropic/claude-opus-4-20250514` (overridden), instructions concatenated
- **Performance advisor**: `enabled: false` (from the user-level file)

## Unsupported Tool Grants Example

```yaml
advisors:
  - name: "Dangerous"
    tools:
      - read
      - write
      - bash
      - edit
```

This produces `unsupportedTools: ["read", "write", "bash", "edit"]` on the
"Dangerous" advisor. No tool is granted.

## Privacy & Security

- `WATCHDOG.yml` files are read locally and are not uploaded as files.
- Instruction text from WATCHDOG.md files is included in the
  reviewer prompt and therefore sent to the advisor model provider. In the
  MVP it is also redacted for secret-like patterns before provider dispatch.
- Tool grants are **not applied** in this release. The reviewer has no
  workspace tool access.
- WATCHDOG.md discovery never walks outside the project root toward the
  session directory. `@path`/`@import` lines are **not** resolved or read in
  the MVP, so no import path can escape anything.
- OMP paths are **opt-in only** (`guidance.ompPaths: true`). The default is
  `false` to avoid activating another tool's private config.

## API Reference

### `src/roster.ts`

```ts
// Discover and parse WATCHDOG.yml/yaml files broad-to-specific.
export async function discoverRoster(
  projectRoot: string,
  sessionDir: string,
  ompPaths: boolean,
): Promise<DiscoveredRoster>

// Check if any advisor has unsupported tool grants.
export function hasUnsupportedTools(roster: DiscoveredRoster): boolean

// Return advisors with unsupported tool grants.
export function advisorsWithUnsupportedTools(
  roster: DiscoveredRoster,
): DiscoveredAdvisor[]
```

### Types

```ts
export interface RosterDiagnostic {
  path: string               // absolute file path
  message: string            // human-readable diagnostic
  severity: "warning" | "error"
}

export interface DiscoveredAdvisor {
  name: string               // display name
  slug: string               // slugified id
  enabled: boolean           // per-advisor toggle
  model?: string             // raw model ref (caller resolves)
  instructions?: string      // merged persona instructions
  unsupportedTools?: string[] // rejected tool names (if any)
}

export interface DiscoveredRoster {
  enabled: boolean           // top-level roster enabled
  advisors: DiscoveredAdvisor[]  // merged advisors in discovery order
  sharedInstructions?: string    // concatenated shared instructions
  diagnostics: RosterDiagnostic[] // all diagnostics from discovery
}
```

## Integration Notes

### Dependency Stance

The `yaml` package (^2.9.0) is a direct **devDependency** in `package.json`,
imported only by `src/roster.ts`; no other module imports it. Because
`src/roster.ts` is not imported from `src/index.ts`, `src/runtime.ts`, or any
other live entrypoint, the shipped plugin entry has zero runtime
dependencies. When wiring Phase 2, it will need to move to a runtime
dependency:

```bash
bun add yaml
```

The import is isolated in `src/roster.ts` - no other module imports `yaml`.

### Runtime Wiring (NOT YET CONNECTED)

**Status: deferred.** `src/roster.ts` is not imported from `src/index.ts`,
`src/runtime.ts`, or any other live entrypoint. Plugin options remain the only
roster source in MVP. When Phase 2 lands, call `discoverRoster()` alongside
`discoverWatchdog()` — a typical integration point in `src/runtime.ts` would be:

```ts
import { discoverRoster } from "./roster.js"

// In the runtime's processCoalesced or similar:
const roster = await discoverRoster(
  projectRoot,
  sessionDir,
  options.guidance.ompPaths,
)
if (roster.diagnostics.length > 0) {
  // Log diagnostics
}
if (hasUnsupportedTools(roster)) {
  // Warn or error
}
```

### No Circular Imports

`src/roster.ts` does not import from `options.ts`, `runtime.ts`, or any other
project module. It only imports from `node:*` builtins and `yaml`. This means
it can be imported by `options.ts`, `runtime.ts`, or any other module without
creating a cycle.
